We need to solve the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267214/assets/2809b78d15a6d3ea95f727b0470fc90009934a3ba6f577592169275333e8316e.svg)

Setting the equations equal to one another and simplifying, we get a quadratic equation:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267214/assets/0161335f522cf20b60b3aabe95092d46d016a1bdb89107f5bcedc41b24dcfc43.svg)

Then, we use the quadratic formula:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267214/assets/d482eb32d8ef80d98f8bc1501828a027fb6247f28c74b9227b8ad488b0692b57.svg)

The square root of a negative number is not a real number, so there are no real solutions. Consequently, the line ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267214/assets/30930f63de8bf94639e0637fe0fc9a000d07ff8ecaadf908b8a8c430105637f1.svg) does not intersect the reciprocal function ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14267214/assets/b47b9ab9cfc0d46f139f26b54e23ead3bf10e8c642627d4981e1441a3da5c970.svg)
